items.rationale: The washing-machine leak qualifies as escape of water under §2.4.2. Section 7.1.7(h) covers necessary residue removal from the affected floor; €65 allows for a small utility room.
Section 7.1.7(h) covers necessary cleaning where the escaped water reached the hallway. The €82 allowance is for the affected floor, not general hallway cleaning.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the leak source and confirming that it no longer discharges, even if the appliance itself is uninsured. Allow €90 for a focused inspection, not appliance servicing.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged skirting
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(a) covers dismantling and disposal of affected fixed finishes. Allow €115 for removing a modest run of skirting and disposing of the debris.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.9 limit replacement to the affected runs at the pre-loss specification. Allow €250 gross for standard skirting, fittings and installation.

items.description: Clean and repaint unaffected upstairs bedroom
items.rationale: Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude work in a separate room with no documented physical damage.

items.description: Measure moisture in both affected floors
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary moisture measurements in the two affected rooms. Allow €165 gross, consistent with the comparable floor and wall-base survey in Case 21.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying in the utility room and hallway. Allow €100 for drying work distinct from equipment hire and separately billed labour; §7.1.8(c) bars duplication.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers necessary equipment hire if not already included in the drying charge. Allow €60 for a modest rental; §7.1.8(d) bars a separate utility charge.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers distinct and necessary trade labour at customary rates. Four hours at €47 gross gives €188, subject to the §7.1.8(c) exclusion for time already billed on earlier lines.

items.description: Measure and dry basement storage room
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) do not extend drying or related moisture measurements to a separate room without documented damage.

Section 5.2.6 covers specialist transport but applies one €1,000 net cap to the unscheduled painting, or €1,190 gross at 19% VAT. Full restoration is estimated to exhaust the cap first; transport would have first call on any remainder.
Assessment is required by §5.2.6 but does not have a separate allowance. It receives only what remains of the €1,190 gross cap after restoration and transport.
Section 5.2.6 covers stabilisation in principle, but this line ranks after restoration, transport and assessment against the same €1,190 gross cap. A balance is unlikely.
Section 5.2.6 applies the unscheduled-item limit to restoration first. Estimated restoration costs reach the €1,000 net limit, yielding €1,190 gross with 19% VAT actually incurred under §7.7.
Section 5.2.6 requires the individual item to have been affected by the insured event. The second painting was not affected.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separately billed administrative and processing charges, and §5.2.6 does not list them as conservation costs.
